results.name: Guinea-Bissau
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a military coup has replaced elected government with unaccountable rule. On November 23-26, 2025, Guinea-Bissau's Military High Command seized power before election results were announced and jailed the opposition leader.

results.name: Ahmedabad
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a single extreme flood is one data point in a 40-part assessment; Ahmedabad's critical band reflects thin, reactive institutional capacity, not one storm.

results.name: DuPont
results.key_finding: Why it matters: one new state lawsuit is a single data point; DuPont's developing-band score already reflects a long PFAS liability history, so the July 2026 New York suit confirms rather than changes the profile.

results.name: Poland
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Poland's in-window signals are mixed and roughly offsetting, so the functional-band score holds.

results.name: Libya
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the accountability step is externally driven (the ICC), not Libya's own conduct, so the critical-band floor score holds.

results.name: Becton Dickinson
results.key_finding: Why it matters: this is a data-integrity flag, not an evidence-driven decline. Becton Dickinson published composite of 54.1 does not match its own stored dimension scores, which produce 42.2 under the canonical formula (an 11.9-point arithmetic discrepancy confirmed by validate-indexes.mjs).

results.name: Hong Kong
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the July 2026 bookseller arrests are the government's own conduct and are consistent with the existing low Boundaries, Accountability, and Integrity scores.

results.name: Ukraine
results.key_finding: Why it matters: rising casualties in Ukraine are harm inflicted ON Ukraine by Russian strikes, not Ukraine's own conduct, so under screening rule 3 they do not lower Ukraine's score.

results.name: Israel
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Israel is already at the absolute floor (0/100); continued in-window conduct confirms the floor and cannot lower it further.

results.name: Palestine
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the Palestinian population and authorities are primarily the victims of in-window harm, not its authors, so under screening rule 3 the developing-band score holds.

results.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the near-floor score reflects a state unable to contain a fast-moving epidemic amid ongoing conflict; the July 2026 Ebola surge confirms that capacity gap.

results.name: Iran
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Iran's own in-window conduct (cross-border strikes on civilian infrastructure) is aggressive, and it is already near the floor, so the score is confirmed at 2.5.

results.name: Russia
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Russia is at the absolute floor (0/100); its in-window conduct - driving a 37% rise in civilian casualties - confirms the floor.

results.name: Haiti
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the Haitian state has lost effective control of most of its capital to gangs; the critical-band score reflects near-total institutional collapse, confirmed by the latest UN data.

results.name: Meta Platforms
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the AI-layoff discrimination suit is one more data point consistent with Meta's existing near-floor score, not a new decline; a single lawsuit does not reset a 40-part assessment.

calibration_note: Becton Dickinson filed as flag-for-review, not downgrade: its published composite (54.1) is an arithmetic error that does not reconstruct from its own dimensions (canonical formula = 42.2, diff 11.9, confirmed by validate-indexes.mjs). Dimensions unchanged; the July FDA recall is a single data point that confirms the profile. DuPont/Meta are researched (not placeholder) scores; single lawsuits/recalls treated as one data point each. Conflict cluster (Ukraine, Israel, Palestine, Iran, Russia, DRC, Haiti) confirmed per screening rule 3 - being attacked/harmed is not the entity's own conduct and does not move the score; floor entities cannot move lower.
